chapter: Dixieland, revival bands and record collectors
title: Jim Crow attitudes and Johnny Bayersdorffer's band
summary: Segregation shaped what people listened to; the interviewer made collectors hear Bayersdorffer's band, whose two best sides he still prizes.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: I'll tell you, that was, Byerstoffer was, I think they only got about four sides out of, two sides? Two. And I still think those were two of the best sides out of New Orleans in the 20s that I'd
ever run across. I always regretted that I never interviewed him, I knew him. Was he? Oh. And he came back, do you remember? No, I don't. He even played at the famous store for a little while.
And nobody, huh, too bad nobody recorded him. Somebody should.
Well, there were tapes of him then, later on. But he, you know, he's gone through the process, having played in big bands and changed his style and everything.
